verdict.line: You lose the laning phase to Kled's hook-and-burst combo, but you win the matchup 53.7% over 136 games because your itemization flips it once Trinity Force comes online.

brief.thesis: Kled's early kit — Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) hook-and-yank, E (Jousting) dash poke, and W (Violent Tendencies) attack-speed burst — lets him force trades and solo kills before Jax has Counter Strike up often enough or any item power to answer, which is why Kled holds both lane and solo-kill advantage. Jax doesn't win the lane phase; he survives it with Doran's sustain and scales past it, because Kled's damage is almost entirely front-loaded into his mounted combo while Jax's damage grows with every item.

theirWindow.when: Kled mounted, W active, full courage
theirWindow.what: W (Violent Tendencies) grants massive attack speed for four attacks with the fourth dealing bonus damage, and he can follow it with Q's hook-yank off cooldown (11/10/9/8/7s). Do not trade into this — if you're caught, time E (Counter Strike) to dodge the empowered autos, including that bonus-damage fourth hit, then land the stun.

yourWindow.what: While dismounted, Kled deals less damage to champions and his Q becomes Pocket Pistol — a ranged knockback with no hook-yank. This is when you commit: W (Empower) into every auto and hold E as a finisher, since his combo is gutted until he restores courage.

runes.keystoneWhy: 75% win rate on this page over a smaller sample. Grasp plus Second Wind is the sustain package that answers Kled's early poke pattern directly — you're not trying to win trades, you're trying to survive them until your items do the winning.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport runs 62.5% over a 32.4% pick rate and fits the scaling plan — Teleport lets you reset after losing the early trades instead of being forced to fight. Exhaust+Flash posts the highest raw win rate (83.3%) on a small sample if you'd rather directly neuter his W all-in burst.

playing.title: Hold E for the fourth auto
playing.detail: Counter Strike dodges all incoming basic attacks while active. Kled's W (Violent Tendencies) gives four empowered attacks with the fourth dealing bonus damage — time your E to eat that whole window and land the stun for free.

playing.title: Don't engage mounted, full-courage Kled
playing.detail: Full courage means his Q hook-yank and W burst are both live. Wait for E (Counter Strike) to be up or for him to be dismounted before you commit.

playing.title: Punish the dismount window hard
playing.detail: Once Skaarl's health depletes, Kled deals less damage to champions and loses his hook-yank entirely. This is your all-in window — W every auto and finish with E.

playing.title: Deny hook angles with minions
playing.detail: Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) has 800 range and yanks you in. Stay behind your wave or at max range so he can't start his combo for free.

playing.title: Empower every short trade
playing.detail: W (Empower) is on a short cooldown (7s down to 3s at max rank) — use it on poke exchanges even when you're not planning to all-in, since it's up far more often than his W burst.

playing.title: Use Q to close, not to open
playing.detail: Leap Strike is 17s at rank 1 — far longer than his E (Jousting) at 13s. Save it to punish his dash on cooldown rather than initiating into a free Joust-away.

playing.title: Play for Trinity Force, not for lane kills
playing.detail: The matchup's math rewards patience: even trades or small losses early are fine, because your empowered autos and Counter Strike stuns start outvaluing his all-in the moment your core item lands.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.
